title: A loop round with bounded heads
statement: Let $B$ and $t$ be natural numbers with $t>0$. Let $body$ and $F$ be finite Boolean Turing machines, let $anchor$ be a state of $body$, let $x,s,next,word$ be Boolean words, let $fuel$ be a configuration of $F$ on input $x$, and let $accepted$ be a Boolean. Start $body$ from the seam configuration with state $anchor$ and word $s$ on tape $0$ (all other work tapes blank). Assume that at every time $u$ with $0<u<t$ its state is not $anchor$; if $accepted$ is true, assume that at time $t$ it has halted and output exactly the one-bit word $[true]$, and otherwise assume that at time $t$ it is exactly the seam configuration with state $anchor$ and word $next$. Assume also that throughout times $u\le t$ this run uses at most $B$ work-tape cells in total, and that every work-tape head of $fuel$ lies between $-B$ and $B$. Then, for the loop-host machine in non-search mode, started in its ready configuration with this body seam, the given word as payload, and fuel $fuel$, there is a time $v$ such that through every time $u\le v$ all work-tape heads lie between $-(B+2|word|+6)$ and $B+2|word|+6$, and either the host is halted at time $v$, or the word admits a successful one-unit debit and at some time $v$ the host configuration is exactly its ready configuration for the seam with state $anchor$ and word $next$, with the debited word as payload and the same fuel configuration. Here a successful debit means the recursive operation that changes the first true bit to false, changing each preceding false bit to true; it fails if the word contains no true bit.
